name: Quirinius
overview: Quirinius was a male figure known for serving as the governor of Syria during the time of the census mentioned at the birth of Jesus. Scripture identifies him specifically in Luke 2:2. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes beyond his official role.
namesAndTitles: The name Quirinius is presented as a proper name without a given meaning in the biblical text. His title, 'Governor of Syria,' translates to '[head of the] garrison,' indicating his authoritative role in regional governance as noted in Luke 2:2.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Quirinius beyond his official position as governor of Syria. No personal or familial connections are documented in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Quirinius holds significance in the biblical narrative as the Roman governor overseeing Syria during the census that prompted Joseph and Mary to travel to Bethlehem, leading to the birth of Jesus. His role situates the nativity within a historical context of Roman administration, confirming the fulfillment of prophecy regarding Jesus' birth location. This connection underscores God's providential orchestration of events surrounding the incarnation.
